findings.actual_failure: OverflowError: Python int too large to convert to C int escapes run_intake_transaction and aborts the drain run with no run report
findings.observation: Liveness probe crashes on an out-of-range numeric lock payload, aborting the drain instead of holding. _pid_is_live catches only ProcessLookupError and OSError, but os.kill raises OverflowError for any pid above INT32_MAX, and _lock_identity's 20-byte bounded read plus int() accepts an all-digit payload above INT32_MAX (ten nines). Reproduced: run_intake_transaction over a temp git repo whose .workspace-repair.lock holds an all-digit payload above INT32_MAX raises OverflowError, escaping run_intake_transaction (its except FileExistsError does not match), then transact_route's defect branch, then drain(), so one such lock aborts the whole run with a traceback and no run report. Contradicts the amended § D1 (no failure of that kind aborts the run), the SKILL.md § 5 sentence this diff ships (an unprobeable payload must yield lock-busy), the function's own docstring (anything the probe cannot rule out is live), and the sibling intent_rename.py _pid_is_dead pattern this code cites, which converts OverflowError into a refusal.
findings.reachable_path: packs/core/.apm/skills/work-intake/scripts/intake_transaction.py _pid_is_live (lines ~278-289): a .workspace-repair.lock whose payload is an all-digit numeric string above INT32_MAX
findings.rule_ref: spec § D1 (AC-0028, AC-0005): no failure of that kind aborts the run; a lock whose payload the probe cannot rule out is treated as live

findings.actual_failure: RuntimeError: Symlink loop escapes _citation_refusal and aborts the drain run with no run report on Python 3.11, instead of the item being held with a citation refusal
evidence_refs: python 3.11.17 reproduction: Path.resolve() on a two-link symlink loop raises RuntimeError; CI pins python-version 3.11 in .github/workflows/build-check.yml
findings.observation: A superseded-closure citation whose path reaches a circular symlink aborts the whole drain run on CI's Python 3.11, instead of the item being held. _citation_refusal resolves the cited path through _confine_member, which calls Path.resolve() and catches only (OSError, ValueError); on Python 3.11 (the version .github/workflows/build-check.yml pins for CI), Path.resolve() raises RuntimeError for symlink loops (CPython #109187, fixed only in 3.13+). Reproduced: a two-link symlink loop at the cited path makes Path.resolve() raise 'RuntimeError: Symlink loop' on Python 3.11.17, escaping _confine_member, _citation_refusal, and drain() — the run aborts with a traceback and no run report, violating the spec's hold-not-abort rule for a citation that fails resolution. On Python 3.13+ resolve() returns the loop path and the citation is refused as citation-path-missing (fail-closed), so the defect is version-dependent. The same _confine_member serves the execution envelope's stored-path confinement (pre-existing, PR #1688), so the fix belongs in _confine_member itself, covering both callers.
findings.reachable_path: packs/core/.apm/skills/project-knowledge/scripts/promotion_drain.py _citation_refusal -> _confine_member (Path.resolve catches OSError, ValueError only); a circular symlink inside the repository at a cited artifact path, under Python 3.11 (CI's version)
findings.rule_ref: security-checklists path-and-file: resolve()-raised RuntimeError on symlink loops (CWE-73 confinement check; the module's tree-walk axis names catching (OSError, RuntimeError) around resolve()); OWASP Top 10:2025 A10 mishandling of exceptional conditions
